evidence: Dimension weights: task tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical in content to the template ([gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05), matching the SKILL.md delivery profile; functional (0.6) outweighs polish+visual (0.4 max non-functional contribution), and score.py:46-48 applies a weighted mean only when gates and the functional floor pass. Per-criterion functional weights (functional/judge.toml:32-38 rule: core legal 2.0 per part, ordinary chat 1.5, small 1.0) re-derive to 44.0 as stated (3+4+4+2+1.5+4+4+2+3+1.5+1.5+1.5+2.5+1.5+4+4). They track the brief, which says walls and retention 'matter more than anything else' (instruction.md para 2): wall criteria (wall_every_route 4, wall_mentions_and_links 4, wall_added_live 2) plus retention (deleted_and_expired_messages 4, timer_changes 4, hold_scope_and_release 2) plus persistence 4 = 24/44 (~55%), plus signin_and_client_scope 3 (signed-out/cross-client denial) = 27/44 (~61%); ordinary chat features (nested_replies, safe_formatting, message_links, unread, live updates 1.5 each; sent_once 2.5; edits 3; search_and_transcript 4) share the rest. No structural or style check sits in functional; polish holds six equal 1.0 binary interaction behaviours, visual four likert criteria with the domain-specific matter_sidebar/retention_marks at 2.0 and transcript/phone at 1.0. Gates carry no reward mass (all_pass, 0.0). Minor observations (not defects): (a) the weight rule classes client scope as 'ordinary' 1.5 although the brief puts client confinement alongside walls ('The same goes for clients...'), arguably understated by 0.5; (b) because the template fixes 0.6/0.2/0.2 while functional has 16 criteria and visual only 4, a single visual likert criterion (matter_sidebar: 0.2*2/6 = 6.7% of reward) carries more reward mass than the strongest single functional criterion (wall_every_route: 0.6*4/44 = 5.5%), and each polish binary (3.3%) more than safe_formatting or nested_replies (2.0%). Counter-test tried: a polished chat that leaks walls only via search snippets loses ~5.5%, which a plainer airtight app can lose through visual mediocrity, so the per-criterion cross-dimension ordering is not strictly 'function above style'; this is a consequence of template-controlled dimension weights (Internal E45: each dimension has its own weightage) and cannot be fixed by task edits without altering template scoring policy, so it is recorded, not failed. Conforming-alternative check: no weight penalises an alternative design (visual matter_sidebar explicitly accepts list-on-own-screen; likert anchors avoid penalising absent unread counts). Risk=true because raw-evidence-index.json states reward discrimination/ranking runs and a full configured grading run are absent for these bytes, so the honest-weight reading is static only and unmeasured.
